findings.title: Split reviews retain only the first part’s usage
findings.description:
Each part now receives a usage record, but `_review()` returns `fold_review_parts(results)`. In `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review_fold.py`, `_metadata()` copies the first part’s metadata and sums only tool calls. Consequently, a successful three-part review records only part 1’s tokens, turns, duration, and cost. The other artifacts are excluded from standalone statistics because they carry `runId`, so their spend disappears from both reports.

Aggregate usage across all parts before returning the folded result, and add a multi-part test with distinct usage values asserting the persisted record and report totals.

findings.title: Failed compactions discard available spend
findings.description:
Usage is stamped only when `session.compact()` succeeds. If its summary dispatch raises a `ProviderError`, the session attaches completed-result telemetry, but this exception handler returns an empty-metadata result and discards it. Spend is also lost if summary capture succeeds and the subsequent reconnect fails, because `SDKExecutionSession.compact()` never returns the captured reply.

Preserve captured telemetry through both failure paths and stamp it on the failed action. Cover provider failure after a completed result and reconnect failure after successful summary capture.

findings.title: Collection-valued costBasis crashes the entire reviews report
findings.description:
`read_frontmatter()` returns arbitrary YAML values. A valid YAML field such as `costBasis: [provider]` produces a list, and testing that value for membership in a set raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. This aborts `sq stats reviews` instead of warning and retaining the row with an unknown basis, as the parser promises.

Validate that the value is a string before the membership check. Add parametrized tests for list and mapping values, asserting a warning and successful report generation.
